why: Replaces PIZERO-98, closed with its answer (no video dropouts; ~0.46 freezes/h). The firmware has changed a lot since, so the next 25 h run is a regression check of the current build, with the Mac kept awake this time. Soak one board while working on another.
Print Screen to a PNG on the card. Independent of everything else and small (a streamed, uncompressed PNG writer, host-tested); it also makes screenshots for the docs and the retrospectives trivial.

Built into the normal firmware since GIME_TIMER went default (f43edd9), but never seen on hardware. Testing it is just running a CoCo 3 timer program at the BASIC prompt; it also settles the reload-quirk revision, which sets the tempo of anything written against it.

Same session, needs the keyboard: play something audible. Two things changed under it (in-spec 60 Hz timing, and the 0.9% shortfall gone), and it is the only way to hear whether PIZERO-121's 8.7 discarded samples a second matter.

The servo has first hardware evidence (2026-09-28: fill climbed 3,063 -> 3,916 toward its set-point, rate easing 48,031 -> 48,005, no underruns or skips) but no long run yet. Its long run is the PIZERO-168 soak: one session proves both.

Still the worst daily-use defect: a keyboard attached after boot never enumerates, which cost us a power cycle mid-measurement today. No longer a freeze suspect, since the soak is clean, so it is a usability fix rather than a stability one.

Demoted from 3 to 9: the mechanism is understood (our symbol stream is legal but the hardest case for a receiver's equalisation, and this monitor fails on colour in one region) and no other sink has shown it. Pair with PIZERO-99; re-raise immediately if a second screen shows it.
Other people's screens, which the kit rests on, and the same session answers whether the fuzz follows the board or the monitor.

Turns vetting into something every build repeats. The pieces exist (156 host tests, the soak harness, the [run]/[aud]/[csg] telemetry), so this is mostly assembly: a firmware build that runs the checks and prints PASS or FAIL with the measured number.
CoCo 3 track, stage 1: a 6809 lockstep correctness harness. Host only, and the precondition for touching the core at all.
CoCo 3 track, stage 2: the 1.79 MHz benchmark and baseline, so the speed work has a target.
CoCo 3 track, stage 3: the speed-up the whole CoCo 3 effort hangs on. Its gate decides whether PIZERO-133 happens.
CoCo 3 track, stage 4, behind the PIZERO-131 gate and the PIZERO-135 decisions.
